questions.question: Connect: Devika Rani (1969), Prithviraj Kapoor (1971, posthumous), Raj Kapoor (1987), Dilip Kumar (1994), Dev Anand (2002).
questions.explanation: India's highest cinema honour; Devika Rani was the first ever recipient (1969).

questions.question: Connect: Raj Kapoor, Dilip Kumar, Dev Anand — three actors who dominated Hindi cinema across the 1950s and 60s.
questions.explanation: The three most popular male stars of the 1950s-60s, each with a distinct style — the showman, the tragedy king, and the evergreen romantic.

questions.question: Connect: Zanjeer (1973), Deewaar (1975), Sholay (1975), Don (1978), Trishul (1978).
questions.explanation: All five scripts were by the Salim Khan-Javed Akhtar partnership that built the angry-young-man canon.

questions.question: Connect: Bishan Singh Bedi (left-arm spin), Bhagwat Chandrasekhar (leg spin), Erapalli Prasanna (off spin), Srinivas Venkataraghavan (off spin).
questions.explanation: The four spinners who carried India's Test attack through the late 1960s and 70s, taking 853 wickets between them.

questions.question: Connect: Kapil Dev (1983 World Cup), MS Dhoni (2007 T20 World Cup, 2011 ODI World Cup, 2013 Champions Trophy), Rohit Sharma (2024 T20 World Cup).
questions.answer: Indian captains who won ICC world titles
accept: indian captains who won an icc trophy
captains who won icc world titles
questions.explanation: The only Indian captains to have lifted a senior ICC world trophy.

questions.question: Connect: Tetley (2000), Corus (2007), Jaguar Land Rover (2008), Air India (2021).
questions.explanation: Four headline takeovers by the Tata Group, ending with Air India returning to the founding family.

questions.question: Connect: Sundar Pichai at Google, Satya Nadella at Microsoft, Arvind Krishna at IBM, Shantanu Narayen at Adobe, Leena Nair at Chanel.
questions.explanation: All five are India-born CEOs of major multinationals.

questions.question: Connect: Haridwar, Kanpur, Prayagraj, Varanasi, Patna.
questions.answer: Cities on the banks of the Ganga
accept: cities on the banks of the ganga
questions.explanation: Five major Indian cities along the Ganga, from the Himalayan foothills (Haridwar) down through the plains to Patna in Bihar. Kolkata is often added to such lists but technically sits on the Hooghly distributary, not the Ganga main stem.

questions.question: Connect: Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura.
questions.answer: The Seven Sister States of Northeast India
accept: seven sister states of northeast india
questions.explanation: The seven contiguous states of Northeast India, a name coined on radio in 1972 by Jyoti Prasad Saikia.

questions.question: Connect: Chandrayaan-1 (2008), Mangalyaan (2013 launch), Chandrayaan-3 (south pole landing, 23 August 2023), Aditya-L1 (launched September 2023).
questions.explanation: Four flagship ISRO missions — to the Moon, Mars and the Sun — that put India among the leading space-faring nations.

questions.question: Connect: Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula, Sahadeva.
questions.explanation: The five sons of Pandu — three by Kunti, twins by Madri — and the heroes of the Mahabharata.

questions.question: Connect: Kuvempu (Kannada, 1967), UR Ananthamurthy (Kannada, 1994), Mahasweta Devi (Bengali, 1996), Girish Karnad (Kannada, 1998), Shrilal Shukla (Hindi, 2009).
questions.explanation: India's highest literary honour, awarded to writers in scheduled Indian languages.

questions.question: Connect: Guru Nanak, Guru Arjan, Guru Tegh Bahadur, Guru Gobind Singh.
questions.explanation: Four of the ten Sikh Gurus — the founder (Nanak), two martyrs (Arjan and Tegh Bahadur), and the tenth and last human Guru (Gobind Singh).

questions.question: Connect: Kabir (north India), Mirabai (Rajasthan), Tukaram (Maharashtra), Andal (Tamil Nadu), Surdas (Braj).
questions.explanation: Devotional poet-saints of the Bhakti movement, writing across centuries and regions in their own languages.

questions.question: Connect: Darjeeling tea, Mysore silk, Banarasi sari, Tirupati laddu, Bikaneri bhujia.
questions.answer: Geographical Indication (GI) tagged products of India
questions.explanation: All five carry a Geographical Indication tag tying the product to its place of origin; Darjeeling tea was India's first GI in 2004.
